doc.title: Plas Johnson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996

title: His book and teaching an improvisation class
summary: A ten-year book project and his first teaching experience, explaining what he does to developed players.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: What’s been your involvement in any jazz education things? You mentioned you were working on a book.
Oh yeah, well I’ve been working on a book for ten years.
It better be good when it comes out.

I’m still putting it out of the computer a page at a time but I’ve got a deadline now and I think I’ll finally have it all out of the computer this month, and then there’s a struggle now to get it published. You asked me to send you a copy so I will. See what you think.
We’ll give it a try, yeah.
In fact I’ll show you some of it today.

I have some pages with me. But it’s been kind of a fun thing. I started teaching an improv class oh about five or six years ago. And it was really my first experience with teaching, with trying to impart to players what I do. Because I had no other teaching experience, I guess why I was there was to play for them and to kind of tell them what I do. And that’s
a whole different way of thinking because most players don’t think about what they do, they just do it.
Yeah. It’s hard to talk about it.

Yeah. Like I’ve had a student say — when I say student, I don’t mean kids I mean players who are already developed because I don’t teach scales and stuff like that — he said, “Well what do you do with your mouth you know when you hit so and so?” And I had to think about it and I had to play it over again and then I said, “well the mouthpiece should be a little further up on your tongue.”
